A squad owns problems from prototype to production, including the maintenance and the on-call rotation for what it ships. You own the execution and will run the squad’s rituals: iteration shaping, prioritization, backlog grooming, and estimation - these are your calls. Owning the call means having a point of view on the tradeoffs behind it, and partnering with your stakeholders to work through the problems that surface along the way. You partner closely with a Product Strategist who spends their time in front of members, coaches, and stakeholders, and who prototypes to test ideas quickly. They own what the squad should build and why. You own whether the squad can deliver it, at what cost, and by when. You set the quality bar and the operational standard for your squad and will be empowered by both tooling and adaptable processes to hold it. About you: You are comfortable being accountable for what your squad ships. You still write code, and you want to. This role ships production work every sprint, off the critical path, in the same codebase and the same agent workflows as your squad, so you feel the friction your people feel first-hand. You are a product engineering leader: you are opinionated about the product you own.

You will lead our move off a legacy ITSM tool to a modern, AI-native platform, then bring service management to teams like HR, Finance, Legal, and Security on whichever platform or platforms fit them best. You will be fluent in ITSM theory, comfortable evaluating tools without bias, and willing to roll up your sleeves to configure, integrate, and ship. Above all, you will care about the people on the other side of every request and work to make getting help easy and seamless. What You Will Do: Lead the migration from our legacy ITSM platform to a modern, AI-native one, from data model, workflow, and catalog design through integrations, cutover, and decommission, with no loss in service levels or employee satisfaction Be the voice of the employee. Design requests, catalog items, and knowledge from the worker's point of view so getting help is easy and frictionless, and use feedback and service data to keep removing friction Own the platform as a product: a single roadmap and backlog, clear intake, and prioritization criteria that every service team can see and trust Govern the service catalog and request fulfillment. The ideal candidate has trained structure prediction models at a leading academic or industry lab and knows where today's models break. You will be a self-directed researcher who moves quickly from hypothesis to trained model to rigorous evaluation.
